changes.before: the Committee today reaffirmed its view that the current 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate remains appropriate
changes.after: the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/4 to 1/2 percent

changes.before: Nonetheless, labor market indicators, on balance, show that underutilization of labor resources has diminished since early this year.
changes.after: A range of recent labor market indicators, including ongoing job gains and declining unemployment, shows further improvement and confirms that underutilization of labor resources has diminished appreciably since early this year.

changes.before: The Committee continues to see the risks to the outlook for economic activity and the labor market as nearly balanced but is monitoring global economic and financial developments.
changes.after: Overall, taking into account domestic and international developments, the Committee sees the risks to the outlook for both economic activity and the labor market as balanced.

The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant only gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run.

changes.before: Market-based measures of inflation compensation moved slightly lower; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
changes.after: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; some survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have edged down.
In light of the current shortfall of inflation from 2 percent, the Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected progress toward its inflation goal.
and it anticipates doing so until normalization of the level of the federal funds rate is well under way

changes.before: Voting against the action was Jeffrey M. Lacker, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points at this meeting.

parsed.rationale: The Committee raised the federal funds target range for the first time, upgraded its labor market assessment and moved risks to fully balanced, a clear change in policy direction. This was partly offset by dovish guidance on only gradual increases, monitoring of the inflation shortfall, and extended reinvestment.

spans.quote: the Committee today reaffirmed its view that the current 0 to 1/4 percent target range for the federal funds rate remains appropriate
Nonetheless, labor market indicators, on balance, show that underutilization of labor resources has diminished since early this year.
The Committee continues to see the risks to the outlook for economic activity and the labor market as nearly balanced but is monitoring global economic and financial developments.
Market-based measures of inflation compensation moved slightly lower; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
Voting against the action was Jeffrey M. Lacker, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points at this meeting.
the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/4 to 1/2 percent

A range of recent labor market indicators, including ongoing job gains and declining unemployment, shows further improvement and confirms that underutilization of labor resources has diminished appreciably since early this year.
Overall, taking into account domestic and international developments, the Committee sees the risks to the outlook for both economic activity and the labor market as balanced.

The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant only gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run.
Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; some survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations have edged down.
In light of the current shortfall of inflation from 2 percent, the Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected progress toward its inflation goal.
and it anticipates doing so until normalization of the level of the federal funds rate is well under way
